transcript: There's a very interesting new play at Playwrights Horizons called In The Amazon Warehouse Parking Lot. It's about a group of queer people working at Amazon trying to navigate a somewhat apocalyptic world. It's science fiction but there are plot elements definitely based on real issues like climate change and isolating, oppressive structures imposed by institutions and capitalism. The themes are super interesting and I thought the writing was funny and genuine. But, for a piece that has such an interesting premise and interesting characters, it's kind of unfocused and slow at times. I just wish more attention was paid to clearly explaining the circumstances of the world they’re in so that there could be a stronger emphasis on how the community the characters have created with one another informs the way that they're navigating the ongoing crisis, both at Amazon and beyond. But even though this production feels little undercooked, I'm glad I saw it because I do think it is ripe with potential and I would love to see this piece continue to develop after its run at Playwrights. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Creator finds the themes interesting and writing funny/genuine but calls it unfocused, slow, and undercooked. Sees potential but doesn't clearly recommend.
